questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $4$ kg block rests on a rough horizontal floor with coefficient of kinetic friction $0.25$. A horizontal force of $30$ N pulls it through $5$ m starting from rest, taking $g = 10$. Find the kinetic energy of the block at the end of this displacement.
questions.explanation: Work done by the applied force is $F s = 30 \times 5 = 150$ J. Kinetic friction is $f = \mu m g = 0.25 \times 4 \times 10 = 10$ N, so friction removes $f s = 10 \times 5 = 50$ J. The kinetic energy at the end is $150 - 50 = 100$ J, which is option B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A stone of mass $2$ kg is thrown vertically upward from the ground with a speed of $20$ m/s. A constant air resistance of $20$ N acts on it throughout its upward motion. Taking $g = 10$, find the maximum height reached by the stone in metres.
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2}(2)(20)^2 = 400$ J. At the highest point the speed is zero, and both gravity and air resistance oppose the displacement $h$, so the total work is $-(mg + 20)h = -40h$. Equating the change in energy gives $400 = 40h$, so $h = 10$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A motor lifts a $40$ kg load through a vertical height of $12$ m at constant speed in $6$ s. The motor has an efficiency of $80\%$. Taking $g = 10$, find the power that must be supplied to the motor.
questions.explanation: Useful work against gravity is $mgh = 40 \times 10 \times 12 = 4800$ J, so the useful output power is $4800 / 6 = 800$ W. With efficiency $0.8$, the input power is $800 / 0.8 = 1000$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $3$ kg block slides on a smooth horizontal table at $4$ m/s and strikes one end of a light spring of spring constant $300$ N/m whose other end is fixed to a wall. Find the maximum compression of the spring in centimetres.
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy of the block is $\frac{1}{2}(3)(4)^2 = 24$ J. At maximum compression the block is momentarily at rest, so the elastic energy stored equals this value: $\frac{1}{2}(300)x^2 = 24$. This gives $x^2 = 0.16$, so $x = 0.4$ m, which is $40$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A spring of spring constant $200$ N/m is compressed by $10$ cm and used to push a $0.5$ kg block, initially at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. Find the speed of the block at the instant it leaves the spring at its natural length.
questions.explanation: The elastic energy stored is $\frac{1}{2}kx^2 = \frac{1}{2}(200)(0.10)^2 = 1$ J. Setting this equal to the kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}(0.5)v^2$ gives $v^2 = 4$, so $v = 2$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A car of mass $800$ kg starts from rest on a level, frictionless road and reaches a speed of $20$ m/s after $10$ s under constant acceleration. Find the average power delivered by the engine over this interval, in kilowatts.
questions.explanation: The final kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2}(800)(20)^2 = 160000$ J, which equals the work done by the engine since the road is frictionless. Dividing by the time gives an average power of $160000 / 10 = 16000$ W, which is $16$ kW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $2$ kg block slides from rest down a smooth incline of vertical height $5$ m and then continues onto a rough horizontal patch with coefficient of kinetic friction $0.5$. Taking $g = 10$, find the distance the block travels on the rough patch before it comes to rest.
questions.explanation: On the smooth incline the block gains kinetic energy $mgh = 2 \times 10 \times 5 = 100$ J by the bottom. On the rough patch kinetic friction is $\mu m g = 0.5 \times 2 \times 10 = 10$ N, so the stopping distance is $d = 100 / 10 = 10$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $10$ kg box starts from rest at the bottom of a smooth incline inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A constant force of $60$ N acts parallel to the incline and pulls the box $4$ m up the slope. Taking $g = 10$, find the kinetic energy of the box at the top in joules.
questions.explanation: Work done by the pulling force is $60 \times 4 = 240$ J. The height gained is $4\sin 30^\circ = 2$ m, so gravity does $-mgh = -10 \times 10 \times 2 = -200$ J of work. The kinetic energy at the top is $240 - 200 = 40$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A car moves at a constant speed of $72$ km/h on a level road. Its engine delivers a steady power of $9$ kW to the wheels. Assuming the resistive force is the only force opposing the motion, find the magnitude of this resistive force.
questions.explanation: Convert the speed to SI units: $72$ km/h $= 72 \times \frac{5}{18} = 20$ m/s. At constant speed the engine power balances the resistive force, so $P = Fv$ gives $F = \frac{9000}{20} = 450$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A bob of mass $0.2$ kg hangs from a light inextensible string of length $2$ m. It is released from rest when the string makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical. Taking $g = 10$, find the tension in the string, in newtons, when the bob passes through the lowest point.
questions.explanation: Energy conservation gives the speed at the bottom: $v^2 = 2gL(1 - \cos 60^\circ) = 2(10)(2)(0.5) = 20$ m$^2$/s$^2$. At the lowest point the net upward force supplies the centripetal acceleration, so $T - mg = \frac{mv^2}{L} = \frac{0.2 \times 20}{2} = 2$ N. Hence $T = 2 + 2 = 4$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $5$ kg block is initially at rest on the ground. A constant vertical upward force of $70$ N acts on it, and the block rises through $2$ m. Taking $g = 10$, find the speed of the block at this height.
questions.explanation: Work done by the $70$ N force is $70 \times 2 = 140$ J, while gravity does $-mgh = -5 \times 10 \times 2 = -100$ J. The kinetic energy at this height is $140 - 100 = 40$ J, so $\frac{1}{2}(5)v^2 = 40$, giving $v^2 = 16$ and $v = 4$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $1$ kg ball is thrown horizontally from the top of a $5$ m high cliff with a speed of $4$ m/s. Neglecting air resistance and taking $g = 10$, find the kinetic energy of the ball just before it reaches the ground, in joules.
questions.explanation: The initial kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2}(1)(4)^2 = 8$ J. Falling $5$ m releases gravitational energy $mgh = 1 \times 10 \times 5 = 50$ J. With no air resistance, the kinetic energy at ground level is $8 + 50 = 58$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A particle is acted on by a force $F = 4x$ N along the $x$-axis, where $x$ is in metres. Find the work done by this force as the particle moves from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$ m.
questions.explanation: The force rises linearly from $0$ N at $x = 0$ to $12$ N at $x = 3$ m. Work equals the area under the force-displacement graph, which is a triangle with area $\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 12 = 18$ J. Using the final force for the whole path would wrongly give $36$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A pump lifts water at a steady rate of $60$ kg per minute from a tank to an outlet $9$ m above it. Taking $g = 10$, find the power required to lift the water, in watts.
questions.explanation: Mass lifted per second is $60 / 60 = 1$ kg/s. Each kilogram gains $gh = 10 \times 9 = 90$ J of potential energy, so the rate of work, which is the power, is $1 \times 90 = 90$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $5$ kg block rests on a smooth horizontal floor. A constant force of $40$ N acts on it at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the horizontal, and the block moves $4$ m along the floor. Find the work done by this force.
questions.explanation: Only the horizontal component $F\cos 60^\circ = 40 \times 0.5 = 20$ N does work along the floor, because the vertical component produces no displacement. Multiplying by the displacement gives $20 \times 4 = 80$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $3$ kg block slides from rest down a rough incline of length $5$ m that makes an angle of $37^\circ$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.25$. Taking $g = 10$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$, find the kinetic energy of the block at the bottom, in joules.
questions.explanation: The vertical drop is $5\sin 37^\circ = 3$ m, so gravity does $mgh = 3 \times 10 \times 3 = 90$ J. The normal force is $mg\cos 37^\circ = 24$ N, so friction is $0.25 \times 24 = 6$ N, which removes $6 \times 5 = 30$ J. The kinetic energy at the bottom is $90 - 30 = 60$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball of mass $0.2$ kg is pressed against a vertical spring of spring constant $400$ N/m, compressing it by $10$ cm, and then released from rest. Taking $g = 10$, find the maximum height the ball rises above its release point.
questions.explanation: The stored spring energy is $\frac{1}{2}kx^2 = \frac{1}{2}(400)(0.10)^2 = 2$ J. The ball starts and ends at rest, so all of this energy becomes gravitational potential energy: $mgH = 2$ J, giving $H = \frac{2}{0.2 \times 10} = 1$ m above the release point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $1200$ kg car moves up a straight road whose slope has $\sin\theta = 0.1$, at a constant speed of $20$ m/s. A resistive force of $500$ N opposes the motion. Taking $g = 10$, find the power delivered by the engine in kilowatts.
questions.explanation: Along the slope the engine must supply $mg\sin\theta + R = 1200 \times 10 \times 0.1 + 500 = 1700$ N. Power is this force times the constant speed, $P = 1700 \times 20 = 34000$ W, which is $34$ kW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $2$ kg block on a smooth horizontal table is tied by a light string passing over a light, smooth pulley at the table edge to a hanging $3$ kg mass. The system is released from rest. Taking $g = 10$, find the speed of the blocks after the hanging mass has descended $1$ m.
questions.explanation: The hanging mass loses potential energy $3 \times 10 \times 1 = 30$ J. Both blocks share the same speed $v$, so the total kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2}(2 + 3)v^2 = 30$ J. This gives $v^2 = 12$ and $v = 2\sqrt{3} \approx 3.46$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $2$ kg particle moves along a straight line starting from rest so that its velocity at time $t$ seconds is $v = 3t$ m/s. Find the instantaneous power delivered to the particle at $t = 2$ s, in watts.
questions.explanation: The acceleration is $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 3$ m/s$^2$, so the net force is $F = ma = 2 \times 3 = 6$ N. At $t = 2$ s the velocity is $v = 6$ m/s, so the power is $P = Fv = 6 \times 6 = 36$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $5$ kg block starts from rest at the bottom of a rough incline of inclination $30^\circ$ and is pushed $3$ m up the incline by a constant force of $60$ N applied parallel to the incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.2$. Taking $g = 10$, find the kinetic energy of the block after this displacement.
questions.explanation: Work done by the pushing force is $60 \times 3 = 180$ J. Gravity removes $mg\sin 30^\circ \times 3 = 75$ J. Friction, with magnitude $\mu mg\cos 30^\circ \times 3 = 15\sqrt{3}$ J, opposes the motion and is subtracted. Therefore $K = 105 - 15\sqrt{3} \approx 79$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $4$ kg body at rest at $x = 0$ is acted on by a force $F = (6 - 2x)$ N along the $x$-axis, with $x$ in metres. Find the speed of the body, in m/s, when it reaches $x = 2$ m.
questions.explanation: The work done is the integral of the force over the displacement: $\int_0^2 (6 - 2x)\,dx = [6x - x^2]_0^2 = 12 - 4 = 8$ J. Equating this to the kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}(4)v^2 = 8$ gives $v^2 = 4$, so $v = 2$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $60$ kg person climbs a flight of $20$ steps, each $20$ cm high, in $10$ s at a steady rate. Taking $g = 10$, find the average power the person develops against gravity.
questions.explanation: The total height climbed is $20 \times 0.20 = 4$ m, so the work done against gravity is $mgh = 60 \times 10 \times 4 = 2400$ J. Dividing by the time of $10$ s gives an average power of $240$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $1$ kg block is released from rest on a smooth incline of angle $30^\circ$, from a point $1.8$ m above the free end of a spring of spring constant $500$ N/m, the distance being measured along the incline. The spring is fixed at the bottom of the incline. Taking $g = 10$, find the maximum compression of the spring in centimetres.
questions.explanation: Along the incline the block descends $(1.8 + x)$ m before the spring is compressed by $x$. Energy conservation gives $mg(1.8 + x)\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$, which is $5(1.8 + x) = 250x^2$. The root $x = 0.2$ m satisfies this, since $250(0.04) = 10 = 5(2.0)$. The maximum compression is therefore $20$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A motor with an input power of $2$ kW has an efficiency of $50\%$ and is used to lift a $100$ kg load at constant speed. Taking $g = 10$, find the speed at which the load is raised.
questions.explanation: The useful output power is $0.5 \times 2000 = 1000$ W. At constant speed this equals the rate of gain of potential energy, $mgv$, so $100 \times 10 \times v = 1000$, giving $v = 1$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of $5$ m above a hard floor and rebounds to a maximum height of $3.2$ m after the bounce. Neglecting air resistance, what percentage of its mechanical energy is lost during the bounce?
questions.explanation: The mechanical energy just before impact is $mg \times 5$ and just after leaving the floor it is $mg \times 3.2$. The energy lost is $mg(5 - 3.2) = 1.8\,mg$, a fraction $1.8 / 5 = 0.36$ of the initial energy. This is $36\%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $500$ g ball tied to a light string of length $1$ m is whirled in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is the minimum needed to keep the string taut. Taking $g = 10$, find the kinetic energy of the ball at the lowest point of the circle.
questions.explanation: At the top the minimum speed satisfies $mg = mv_t^2 / R$, so $v_t^2 = gR = 10$ and the kinetic energy there is $\frac{1}{2}(0.5)(10) = 2.5$ J. Falling through $2R = 2$ m to the bottom adds $mg(2R) = 0.5 \times 10 \times 2 = 10$ J, so the kinetic energy at the bottom is $2.5 + 10 = 12.5$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $0.5$ kg object moves along the $x$-axis so that its speed is $v = 2\sqrt{x}$ m/s, where $x$ is in metres. Find the work done by the net force as the object moves from $x = 1$ m to $x = 4$ m, in joules.
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy at position $x$ is $\frac{1}{2}(0.5)(2\sqrt{x})^2 = x$ J. The work done by the net force equals the change in kinetic energy, so $W = K(4) - K(1) = 4 - 1 = 3$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A uniform chain of total mass $4$ kg and length $2$ m lies on a horizontal table with $0.5$ m of it hanging over the edge. Taking $g = 10$, find the minimum work needed to pull the hanging part slowly back onto the table.
questions.explanation: The hanging part has mass $4 \times \frac{0.5}{2} = 1$ kg. Its centre of mass is $0.25$ m below the table top, so raising it onto the table requires $W = mgh = 1 \times 10 \times 0.25 = 2.5$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $2$ kg block initially at rest on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of kinetic friction $0.5$, is pushed by a force of $40$ N directed $37^\circ$ below the horizontal. The block moves $5$ m. Taking $g = 10$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$, find the kinetic energy of the block at the end, in joules.
questions.explanation: The normal reaction is $mg + F\sin 37^\circ = 20 + 24 = 44$ N, so kinetic friction is $0.5 \times 44 = 22$ N. Work done by the push is $40 \times 0.8 \times 5 = 160$ J and work done by friction is $-22 \times 5 = -110$ J. The kinetic energy is $160 - 110 = 50$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $1$ kg bead is released from rest at the level of the centre of a fixed smooth circular track of radius $1$ m and slides on the inner surface down to the lowest point of the circle. Taking $g = 10$, find the normal force exerted by the track on the bead at the lowest point.
questions.explanation: Energy conservation over a height $R = 1$ m gives $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgR$, so $v^2 = 2gR = 20$ m$^2$/s$^2$. At the bottom $N - mg = \frac{mv^2}{R}$, so $N = 10 + 20 = 30$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $5$ kg body initially at rest on a frictionless horizontal floor is pulled by a constant horizontal force of $10$ N. Find the work done by this force during the first $3$ s, in joules.
questions.explanation: The acceleration is $a = F/m = 2$ m/s$^2$, so the displacement in $3$ s is $\frac{1}{2}(2)(3)^2 = 9$ m. The work done is $Fs = 10 \times 9 = 90$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $2$ kg block is projected up a rough incline inclined at $37^\circ$ to the horizontal with a kinetic energy of $64$ J at the bottom. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.25$. Taking $g = 10$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$, find the distance travelled up the incline before the block momentarily comes to rest.
questions.explanation: For each metre travelled up the slope, gravity removes $mg\sin 37^\circ = 12$ N of energy and friction removes $\mu mg\cos 37^\circ = 0.25 \times 20 \times 0.8 = 4$ N, a total of $16$ N. Setting $16d = 64$ gives $d = 4$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A light spring of spring constant $400$ N/m is initially stretched by $5$ cm from its natural length. An external agent then stretches it slowly until its extension is $15$ cm. Find the work done by the external agent in joules.
questions.explanation: The work done in stretching a spring from extension $x_1$ to extension $x_2$ is $\frac{1}{2}k(x_2^2 - x_1^2)$. Substituting $k = 400$ N/m, $x_2 = 0.15$ m and $x_1 = 0.05$ m gives $200(0.0225 - 0.0025) = 200 \times 0.02 = 4$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $3$ kg block is pulled up a smooth incline of angle $30^\circ$ by a force parallel to the incline, so that it moves at a constant speed of $2$ m/s. Taking $g = 10$, find the power delivered by this pulling force.
questions.explanation: At constant speed the pulling force equals the component of weight along the incline: $F = mg\sin 30^\circ = 3 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 15$ N. The power is $P = Fv = 15 \times 2 = 30$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A uniform solid sphere of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is released from rest at the top of a rough incline of inclination $\theta$ and height $h$, and rolls without slipping to the bottom. Which of the following statements are correct?
options: A) The speed at the bottom is $v = \sqrt{\frac{10gh}{7}}$
B) The translational kinetic energy is $\frac{5}{7}$ of the total kinetic energy at the bottom
C) The linear acceleration of the centre of mass is $g\sin\theta$
D) The net work done by static friction on the sphere is zero
questions.explanation: Energy conservation gives $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{5}mR^2\right)\frac{v^2}{R^2} = \frac{7}{10}mv^2$, so $v = \sqrt{\frac{10gh}{7}}$ and A is correct. The translational share is $\frac{1/2}{7/10} = \frac{5}{7}$, so B is correct. The acceleration is $\frac{5}{7}g\sin\theta$, not $g\sin\theta$, so C is wrong. In rolling without slipping the contact point is instantaneously at rest, so static friction does zero net work and D is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A bob of mass $m$ is attached to a light string of length $L$ and released from rest with the string making an angle $\theta$ with the vertical. Which of the following statements are correct?
options: A) The speed of the bob at the lowest point is $\sqrt{2gL(1 - \cos\theta)}$
B) The tension in the string at the lowest point is $mg(3 + 2\cos\theta)$
C) When $\theta = 60^\circ$, the tension at the lowest point is $2mg$
D) The tension at the instant of release is $mg$
questions.explanation: Energy conservation gives $v^2 = 2gL(1 - \cos\theta)$, so A is correct. At the bottom $T - mg = \frac{mv^2}{L} = 2mg(1 - \cos\theta)$, so $T = mg(3 - 2\cos\theta)$, which makes B wrong. For $\theta = 60^\circ$ this gives $T = mg(3 - 1) = 2mg$, so C is correct. At release the speed is zero, so $T = mg\cos\theta$, not $mg$, making D wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A vehicle of mass $m$ starts from rest on a smooth horizontal track and is driven by an engine that delivers a constant power $P$ at all times. Which of the following statements are correct for any time $t > 0$?
options: D) The displacement is proportional to $t$
questions.explanation: Constant power means $\frac{dK}{dt} = P$, so $K = Pt$ and C is correct. Then $v = \sqrt{2Pt/m}$, making A correct. Differentiating, $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \sqrt{\frac{P}{2mt}}$, so B is correct. The displacement is $x = \int v\,dt = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\,t^{3/2}$, which grows as $t^{3/2}$ and not linearly, so D is wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball is dropped from rest at height $h$ above a horizontal floor. Each collision with the floor has coefficient of restitution $e$, where $0 < e < 1$. Neglect air resistance and assume the ball bounces indefinitely. Which of the following statements are correct?
options: A) The height reached after the first bounce is $eh$
B) The fraction of mechanical energy lost in the first bounce is $1 - e^2$
C) The total distance travelled before coming to rest is $h\frac{1 + e}{1 - e}$
D) For $e = 0.5$, the total distance travelled before coming to rest is $\frac{5}{3}h$
questions.explanation: After each bounce the rebound height is multiplied by $e^2$, so the first rebound height is $e^2h$ and A is wrong. The ball keeps $e^2$ of its energy at each impact, so the fraction lost is $1 - e^2$, making B correct. The total distance is $h + 2h(e^2 + e^4 + \cdots) = h\frac{1 + e^2}{1 - e^2}$, so C is wrong. For $e = 0.5$ this equals $h\frac{1.25}{0.75} = \frac{5}{3}h$, making D correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A light string connects a $2$ kg block on a smooth horizontal table to a hanging $3$ kg block. The string passes over a uniform solid disc pulley of mass $2$ kg and radius $R$ that turns without slipping on the string. The system is released from rest. Taking $g = 10$, which of the following statements are correct?
options: A) After the hanging block descends $1$ m, its speed is $\sqrt{10}$ m/s
B) If the pulley's mass were neglected, the speed after descending $1$ m would be $\sqrt{12}$ m/s
C) The rotational kinetic energy of the pulley equals half the translational kinetic energy of the hanging block
D) The block on the table carries one-half of the total kinetic energy of the system
questions.explanation: Energy gives $3 \times 10 \times 1 = 30 = \frac{1}{2}(2 + 3 + 1)v^2$, where the pulley's rotational energy $\frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{4}Mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}v^2$ is included, so $v^2 = 10$ and A is correct. Ignoring the pulley gives $30 = \frac{1}{2}(5)v^2$, so $v^2 = 12$ and B is correct. The pulley's rotational energy is $\frac{1}{2}v^2$, while half the hanging block's energy is $\frac{3}{4}v^2$, so C is wrong. The table block holds $v^2 = 10$ J out of $30$ J, which is one-third, so D is wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A particle of mass $2$ kg starts from rest at $x = 0$ and moves along the $x$-axis under a force $F = (6x - 3x^2)$ N, where $x$ is in metres. Find its speed when it reaches $x = 2$ m.
questions.explanation: The work done is $\int_0^2 (6x - 3x^2)\,dx = [3x^2 - x^3]_0^2 = 12 - 8 = 4$ J. Equating this to the kinetic energy gives $\frac{1}{2}(2)v^2 = 4$, so $v^2 = 4$ and $v = 2$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A solid cylinder of mass $2$ kg and radius $0.5$ m rests on a rough horizontal floor. A constant horizontal force of $6$ N acts on its centre of mass, and the cylinder starts from rest and rolls without slipping through $4$ m. Find its speed, in m/s, at the end of this displacement.
questions.explanation: Work done by the applied force is $6 \times 4 = 24$ J. Static friction does no net work during pure rolling. The kinetic energy of rolling is $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}mR^2\right)\frac{v^2}{R^2} = \frac{3}{4}mv^2 = 1.5v^2$. Thus $1.5v^2 = 24$ gives $v^2 = 16$ and $v = 4$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A block of mass $2$ kg slides from rest down a rough incline of length $5$ m inclined at $37^\circ$ to the horizontal, with coefficient of kinetic friction $0.25$. Taking $g = 10$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$, find the heat generated at the contact surface during the slide.
questions.explanation: Friction is $\mu mg\cos 37^\circ = 0.25 \times 20 \times 0.8 = 4$ N, and the displacement along the incline is $5$ m, so the heat is $4 \times 5 = 20$ J. As a check, the total drop in potential energy $mg \times 5\sin 37^\circ = 60$ J equals the heat plus the kinetic energy $40$ J at the bottom.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A block of mass $2$ kg is placed gently on a long horizontal conveyor belt moving at a constant speed of $3$ m/s. The coefficient of kinetic friction between block and belt is $0.3$, and the block accelerates until it reaches the belt speed. Find the total work done by the motor driving the belt during this process.
questions.explanation: The friction force is $\mu mg = 0.3 \times 2 \times 10 = 6$ N and the block's acceleration is $\mu g = 3$ m/s$^2$, so slipping lasts $t = v/a = 1$ s. The belt moves $vt = 3$ m in this time, so the motor does $6 \times 3 = 18$ J of work. Half of this becomes the block's kinetic energy ($9$ J) and half is dissipated as heat ($9$ J).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body of mass $2$ kg rests on a smooth horizontal floor. From $t = 0$ onward a horizontal force $F = 4t$ N acts on it, where $t$ is in seconds. Find the work done by this force in the first $3$ s.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is $a = F/m = 2t$ m/s$^2$, so the velocity is $v = \int_0^t 2t\,dt = t^2$. The kinetic energy at time $t$ is $\frac{1}{2}(2)t^4 = t^4$, which equals the work done. At $t = 3$ s this gives $3^4 = 81$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball is dropped from rest at a height of $16$ m above a floor and bounces repeatedly, with coefficient of restitution $e = \frac{1}{2}$ at every impact. Neglecting air resistance, find the height the ball reaches after its third rebound from the floor.
questions.explanation: Each rebound multiplies the height by $e^2 = \frac{1}{4}$, so after the third rebound the height is $he^6 = 16 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^6 = \frac{16}{64} = 0.25$ m. Using $e^3$ instead would give $2$ m, and stopping after two rebounds would give $1$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A bob of mass $m$ is attached to a light inextensible string of length $L$ and is released from rest when the string is horizontal. Give the integer value of the ratio $T/(mg)$, where $T$ is the tension in the string at the lowest point.
questions.explanation: Energy conservation from the horizontal position gives $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgL$, so $v^2 = 2gL$. At the lowest point $T - mg = \frac{mv^2}{L} = 2mg$, hence $T = 3mg$ and the ratio is $3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A thin spherical shell of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is released from rest at a height of $0.75$ m on a rough incline and rolls without slipping to the bottom. Taking $g = 10$, find the speed of its centre of mass at the bottom, in m/s.
questions.explanation: Energy conservation gives $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}mR^2\right)\frac{v^2}{R^2} = \frac{5}{6}mv^2$. Thus $v^2 = \frac{6gh}{5} = \frac{6 \times 10 \times 0.75}{5} = 9$, so $v = 3$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A particle of mass $1$ kg moves along the $x$-axis under a conservative force with potential energy $U(x) = x^2 - 4x$ joules, where $x$ is in metres. It is released from rest at $x = 0$. Find the value of $x$, in metres, at which its speed is maximum.
questions.explanation: The speed is maximum where the potential energy is minimum, since the total energy is fixed. Setting $\frac{dU}{dx} = 2x - 4 = 0$ gives $x = 2$ m. Check: $U(2) = 4 - 8 = -4$ J is the lowest value, so the kinetic energy there is $0 - (-4) = 4$ J and the speed is $\sqrt{2 \times 4} = 2\sqrt{2}$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A thin hoop of mass $1$ kg and radius $0.4$ m rolls without slipping up a rough incline inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. At the bottom the centre of mass of the hoop has a speed of $5$ m/s. Taking $g = 10$, find the distance, in metres, that the hoop travels up the incline before it momentarily stops.
questions.explanation: At the bottom the total kinetic energy of the hoop is $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}mR^2\frac{v^2}{R^2} = mv^2 = 25$ J. At the highest point the hoop has risen a height $h$, so $mgh = 25$ gives $h = 2.5$ m. The distance along the incline is $s = h / \sin 30^\circ = 2.5 / 0.5 = 5$ m.
